newsitem.title: USA: Tiny U.S. transplant patient dies after two months.
newsitem.headline: Tiny U.S. transplant patient dies after two months.

text.p: Cheyenne Pyle, who became the world's youngest heart transplant recipient two months ago, has lost her fight for survival after the sudden onset of severe complications, hospital officials said on Friday.
"She died at 2:10 p.m. EST Thursday afternoon," a spokesman for the University of Miami/Jackson Children's Hospital said.

Cheyenne, who was born in November with a severe heart defect, was delivered by caesarean section and received her new heart in her first few hours of life from a stranger whose identity has not been revealed.

Doctors were optimistic immediately after the operation, but Cheyenne had kidney problems and her aorta narrowed as her body struggled to grow and she fought the body's natural tendency to reject the new heart.

On Thursday, the 7-pound (3.2-kg) girl's major organs apparently gave up, in a rapid decline that surprised the medical staff, said Dr. Lee Ann Pearse, pediatric cardiologist and medical director of the pediatric cardiac transplant programme at the hospital.

"This happened so fast that despite everything that was being done for her she just continued to deteriorate," she said. "This is totally a surprise to everybody, it was totally unexpected what happened."

Pearse said everyone was shaken by Cheyenne's death and that her team would use the experience to learn more about transplants, particularly into someone so young. She said the doctors did not yet know what had caused the sudden decline. An autopsy was planned.

The child's parents were called to the hospital from their home in Fort Lauderdale when it became obvious that Cheyenne's problems were especially serious. She spent her last moments cradled in her parents' arms.
